reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes paid cryptocurrency mining-share tiers while presenting a one-time payment as generating continuing returns and offering recurring commissions for referred participants' repurchases. It also directs viewers toward participant contributions, additional pool shares, and ProBuilder status within the promoted network. The displayed commission history, wallet interface, and external signup direction support the described promotional mechanism, while the separate CoinPay payday and free-spins advertisement are not established as connected offers.

citations.quote: If you guys will give me the money for the equipment, I'll mine the Bitcoin and we'll split up all the Bitcoin.
this is pay one time but get paid forever and ever and ever and ever
if you do refer other people every time that they make a repurchase you're getting paid again and again and again and again on all of those people
in my downline, I have about 30,000 people

opening.argument: Judge the speaker's claims in context. He describes CoinPay's prospects as a possibility, not an accomplished result, and says he does not yet have a date for the proposed trip. He also distinguishes an optional merchant activity from joining the network and says Club Coin is given away rather than sold. Those qualifications matter: the presentation contains promotional optimism, but it does not treat every proposed benefit or activity as certain or mandatory.

citations.quote: This literally could make us the next Visa or MasterCard.
I don't have a date yet.
you don't have to sign up a merchant to be in BigClub network it's not a mandatory thing
we give Club coin away for free there is no likewe don't sell it at all.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The quoted phrase about being paid forever is emphatic, but the opening treats it as a guaranteed outcome without addressing the speaker's stated mechanism: part of mined Bitcoin goes back toward equipment and additional shares. Likewise, recurring referral payments are described as conditional on other people making repurchases. Neither quotation alone establishes that those conditions will occur or that the speaker concealed them.

citations.quote: a portion of everybody's Bitcoin that you're mining has to go back in to help buy
if you do refer other people every time that they make a repurchase you're getting paid again and again and again and again on all of those people

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Uncertainty about CoinPay or a trip does not qualify the mining pitch. The speaker explicitly describes paying once and getting paid indefinitely, then adds repeated payments tied to referred participants' repurchases. Optional merchant signup and free Club Coin concern different activities; they do not remove the paid mining-share offer shown on screen.

opening.argument: Much of this webinar walks viewers through how to understand and inspect cryptocurrency. The speaker states an aim of explaining Bitcoin, recommends a separate introductory video, and demonstrates a blockchain explorer's transactions and blocks. He also says viewers can inspect the live websites themselves. A judge should account for that substantial instructional content instead of treating every screen demonstration as a request to purchase.

citations.quote: today what I would like to do is really help everyone to understand bitcóin and what the club network is all about
blockchain info actually is a blockchain Explorer and it tracks Bitcoin
when you're using a live website and now you can go look at that live website on your own

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies real sales language, but it omits the speaker's explicit invitation to learn Bitcoin basics before continuing and his walkthrough of independently inspectable blockchain information. The existence of a mining-share page does not make those demonstrations fictitious. The question is the presentation's character as a whole, not whether it ever discusses a paid offering.

citations.quote: if you can stop the webinar if you're watching the recording and go find this video and watch this video first
here is blockchain.info. So these are the transactions for Bitcoin. These are the blocks of Bitcoin

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The Bitcoin demonstrations provide background for a specific paid offer; they do not displace it. The speaker moves from explaining the network to asking participants to fund equipment in exchange for mined Bitcoin, while the displayed page offers mining-pool shares for purchase. He then describes indefinite payments and recurring referral compensation. Those are central claims about participation, not merely instruction on using a blockchain explorer.

citations.quote: If you guys will give me the money for the equipment, I'll mine the Bitcoin and we'll split up all the Bitcoin.
this is pay one time but get paid forever and ever and ever and ever
if you do refer other people every time that they make a repurchase you're getting paid again and again and again and again on all of those people

opening.argument: The described transaction has a concrete commercial explanation: members contribute toward mining equipment and divide mined Bitcoin. The speaker even compares operating costs for older and newer miners, and the page presents priced mining-pool shares. Referral compensation is disclosed rather than hidden. These materials establish an offer and a compensation structure, but they do not establish that equipment was never acquired, that mining never occurred, or that the displayed account entries were fabricated. A paid service with referral commissions should be assessed on what is shown, not on an assumed failure to deliver.

citations.quote: If you guys will give me the money for the equipment, I'll mine the Bitcoin and we'll split up all the Bitcoin.
the electric for one pedahash of S3 or S4 amp minors was about $56,000 a month the electricity for one pettahash of S nine-amp miners is about sixty five hundred dollars a month
if you do refer other people every time that they make a repurchase you're getting paid again and again and again and again on all of those people

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution accurately identifies a purchase and downline commissions. But a purchase page does not establish whether the purchased service was delivered, and an account-history screen does not establish the underlying source or validity of its entries. The speaker's equipment-funding explanation supplies an ordinary reason participants would contribute money; the opening does not disprove that explanation.

citations.quote: If you guys will give me the money for the equipment, I'll mine the Bitcoin and we'll split up all the Bitcoin.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Proof that mining failed is not necessary to identify what this video promotes. Its purchase page offers mining-pool shares, and the speaker presents a one-time payment as yielding continuing shares and payments. He also says referred participants' repurchases generate repeated compensation and describes a large downline. Calling the proposed use of funds equipment financing does not neutralize those return and recruitment claims.
